pick.headline: Carter imposes grain embargo on the USSR
pick.summary: On January 4, 1980, President Carter announced a partial embargo on grain sales to the Soviet Union and other measures in response to the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.
pick.significance: The embargo marked the end of detente in practical terms. It also hurt American farmers and was lifted by Reagan in 1981.
pick.fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of January 7, 1980, grouped Prague radio commentary on Carter's "anti-Soviet" television speech, listing his measures including halting grain deliveries to the USSR, and casting them as abandoning detente for reelection purposes.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Eastern Europe, Vol. II No. 004, 7 January 1980

alternates.headline: US Navy F-14s shoot down two Libyan MiGs
alternates.summary: On January 4, 1989, two US Navy F-14s from the carrier John F. Kennedy shot down two Libyan MiG-23 fighters over the Mediterranean off Libya.
alternates.significance: It came amid US charges that Libya was building a chemical-weapons plant at Rabta. Tripoli called the jets unarmed reconnaissance planes; Washington said they had acted with hostile intent.
alternates.fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of January 4, 1989, opened its review with the first monitored Libyan reaction: a Tripoli radio statement calling the U.S. Navy downing of two Libyan planes a "premeditated attack" on a routine reconnaissance patrol.
